problem.title: Migrate a Blocking Spring Boot Service to Java Virtual Threads Without Pinning
problem.prompt: After enabling Java 21 virtual threads in a Spring Boot API that fans out to 3 REST services and Postgres, P99 latency spikes under load and JFR shows `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events. Diagnose and fix.

spark.summary: Diagnose carrier-thread pinning, HikariCP connection exhaustion, and ThreadLocal memory bloat when enabling Java 21+ Virtual Threads on a high-throughput Spring Boot service.
spark.keyTakeaway: Enable spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true, swap synchronized I/O guards for ReentrantLock, bound downstream fan-out with Semaphores, and replace ThreadLocal caches with ScopedValue.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** After enabling Java 21 Virtual Threads (`spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`) in a Spring Boot API fanning out to **3 REST services and Postgres** at **10,000+ req/s**, p99 latency spikes under load and JFR emits `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts synchronized Pinning vs. ReentrantLock Unmounting (VirtualThread #1 -> OS Carrier (Core 1) -> VirtualThread #2 -> Postgres / REST); Unmounted I/O Fan-Out with Structured Concurrency & Bulkheads (Tomcat (VT Enabled) -> ReentrantLock -> Semaphore / Hikari -> StructuredTaskScope).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Simply flipping `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true` without auditing JDBC drivers, `synchronized` blocks, `ThreadLocal`s, and HikariCP pool sizes leaves. Migrate Spring Boot imperative services safely to 10,000+ RPS on Java 21: **Eliminate Pinning**: Enable `-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=full` / JFR `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` in staging.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Virtual threads bridge imperative simplicity with reactive scalability: **BFF & API Aggregators**: Fanning out to multiple REST/gRPC/DB backends concurrently with `StructuredTaskScope`.

learningJourney.title: Why Virtual Threads & Pinning Prevention Matter
learningJourney.explanation: After enabling Java 21 Virtual Threads (`spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`) in a Spring Boot API fanning out to **3 REST services and Postgres** at **10,000+ req/s**, p99 latency spikes under load and JFR emits `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events. While keeping imperative JDBC/`RestClient` code, we must eliminate carrier-thread pinning and bound downstream fan-out.
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Why Virtual Threads & Pinning Prevention Matter works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Real-World Impact of Carrier-Thread Pinning
learningJourney.explanation:
In Java 21, virtual threads are multiplexed onto a small pool of OS carrier threads (sized to CPU cores):

1. **Carrier Pinning (`synchronized`)**: Blocking on JDBC/HTTP inside a `synchronized` block pins the virtual thread to its OS carrier thread—starving all other virtual threads.
2. **Downstream Pool Exhaustion**: Spawning 10,000+ concurrent virtual threads without a bulkhead slams Postgres `max_connections`.
3. **ThreadLocal Memory Bloat**: Legacy `ThreadLocal` buffers (`SimpleDateFormat`, byte arrays) duplicated across 100k virtual threads exhaust heap.

sectionDiagram.title: synchronized Pinning vs. ReentrantLock Unmounting

events.label: Pinned! VT#2 starved waiting for carrier
VT#1 unmounts on I/O -> VT#2 runs on carrier!

sectionDiagram.summary: Replacing synchronized around blocking I/O with ReentrantLock lets virtual threads unmount cleanly from OS carriers.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Real-World Impact of Carrier-Thread Pinning under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Naive Solution (and Why It Breaks)
learningJourney.explanation: Simply flipping `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true` without auditing JDBC drivers, `synchronized` blocks, `ThreadLocal`s, and HikariCP pool sizes leaves `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` stalls intact and causes HikariCP `connectionTimeout` storms when 10,000 virtual threads compete for 20 DB connections.
learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Naive Solution under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise Solution: `ReentrantLock`, `Semaphore` Bulkheads & `ScopedValue`
learningJourney.explanation:
Migrate Spring Boot imperative services safely to 10,000+ RPS on Java 21:

- **Eliminate Pinning**: Enable `-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=full` / JFR `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` in staging; replace `synchronized` blocks guarding I/O (and upgrade older JDBC/logging libraries) with `ReentrantLock`.
- **Bound Downstream Concurrency**: Never pool virtual threads (`newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()`); use `Semaphore` bulkheads and `StructuredTaskScope.ShutdownOnFailure` for the 3-way REST + Postgres fan-out.
- **Replace `ThreadLocal` with `ScopedValue`**: Pass request/trace context via immutable `ScopedValue`s instead of heavy per-thread `ThreadLocal` caches.

cards.label: ReentrantLock
cards.detail: Allows JVM to park/unmount virtual thread during I/O wait.

cards.label: Structured Fan-Out
cards.detail: ShutdownOnFailure cancels remaining REST calls if one fails.

cards.label: ScopedValue
cards.detail: Zero-copy immutable context inherited by child virtual threads.

cards.label: JFR Audit
cards.detail: Monitor jdk.VirtualThreadPinned events in CI load tests.

learningJourney.title: Where Virtual Threads Apply in System Design
learningJourney.explanation:
Virtual threads bridge imperative simplicity with reactive scalability:

- **BFF & API Aggregators**: Fanning out to multiple REST/gRPC/DB backends concurrently with `StructuredTaskScope`.
- **High-Concurrency Spring Boot Microservices**: Replaces complex WebFlux reactive chains when libraries are blocking.
- **Legacy JDBC Services**: Scales connection-waiting concurrency without rewriting SQL layers.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why does `synchronized` around a blocking JDBC call degrade throughput under Java 21 Virtual Threads?

options.text: Entering a `synchronized` monitor pins the virtual thread to its OS carrier thread, preventing other virtual threads from using that core during I/O
options.feedback: Correct: replacing `synchronized` with `ReentrantLock` allows the virtual thread to unmount cleanly while waiting on I/O.

options.text: Java 21 throws `UnsupportedOperationException` on `synchronized` inside virtual threads
options.feedback: It still executes, but pins the carrier thread.

options.text: JDBC drivers automatically bypass `synchronized` blocks on virtual threads
options.feedback: JDBC drivers using `synchronized` internally (older versions) are a common source of pinning.

_nextProblem.title: Mitigating Serverless Cold-Start Latency Spikes
_nextProblem.prompt: A Java 21 Spring Boot checkout API on AWS Lambda (and Cloud Run for EU) normally handles 150 RPS at 45 ms p95. When marketing push notifications trigger a 3,000 RPS spike within 10 seconds, 400+ concurrent cold starts fire simultaneously. Each cold start takes 3.4 seconds (JVM + Spring context + RDS Postgres TLS handshake), breaching the 2 s API Gateway timeout and exhausting Postgres max_connections (500).

_problemQuestions.prompt: A user edits their bio and refreshes the page, only to see the old bio for 2 seconds because the read hit a lagging replica. Which consistency guarantee was violated?

options.explanation: Read-Your-Writes ensures a client always observes its own completed writes.
The write was durable on the primary; the replica simply lagged.
Atomicity governs all-or-nothing commit, not cross-replica visibility.

_problemQuestions.prompt: Why does placing `request_timestamp` at the very beginning of a 3,000-token system prompt hurt latency and cost?

options.explanation: BPE still tokenizes the text normally.

options.text: It invalidates prefix/KV caching for all subsequent 3,000 tokens on every request
options.explanation: Correct! Prefix KV caching requires an exact token match from index 0 onward.
Output length is unaffected; Prefill cache reuse is what breaks.
